results.reason: Issue 1 says the Renewal Notice deadline (~Aug. 16, 2026) passed with no notice shown. It says the agreement expires Nov. 14, before the Nov. 30 closing, and that the MIPA § 3.12(c) 'through November 2029' rep and Schedule 3.12 are inaccurate, exposing Sellers to indemnity and fraud claims.

Issue 2 identifies the 100% sale as a Change of Control (§ 1.3(a)) requiring prior written consent (§ 14.2), with a termination right (§ 14.3). It notes the consent is omitted from Schedule 3.6, so it falls outside § 6.4 and § 7.1(d). It recommends obtaining the consent before Closing and adding it to Schedule 3.6.

Issue 6 notes the Side Letter redefines Territory to add NY and VA and that the Side Letter takes precedence under § 19.4. It explains Harrow Creek carries non-compete burdens in six states but has exclusivity in only four, and recommends conforming the territories. The response hedges on whether the expanded definition controls, but it treats the six-state non-compete as the operative risk.

Issue 6 identifies the Side Letter's NY law and NY County forum against the Delaware law and Wilmington forum (§§ 18.1, 18.2). It explains disputes could be split between two courts and two bodies of law, and recommends aligning law and forum with Delaware.
The Key Dates table and Issue 1 state that the Initial Term ends Nov. 14, 2026.
Target Closing is stated as Nov. 30, 2026 (MIPA § 2.2).
Issue 6 states the Distribution Agreement Territory is DE, MD, NJ and PA only (§ 1.12).
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner, and each issue has Where, Issue, Why it matters and Recommendation sections.
Issues are labeled 'Most Significant First' and ranked Critical, High, Medium, then Lower. Part 4 lists items to raise promptly with the client and with Quillon's counsel.
The response states there is no auto-renewal and that a notice delivered now would be late. The protective notice is framed only as a weak fallback.
The response expressly states that Schedule 3.6 omits Velloran and that the consent covenant and closing condition do not reach it.
